name: Professor Mack's Chin Reducer and Beautifier

card.summary: Professor Mack's Chin Reducer and Beautifier was an 1890s cord-and-strap device advertised to remove double chins and slim the jawline.
card.note: Historical advertisement; no test results survive in the material consulted.

quick.overview:
Professor Mack's Chin Reducer and Beautifier was a head-and-chin strap apparatus with cords, advertised in the 1890s to eliminate and efface double chins and reduce "enlarged glands". The ad promised the resiliency and freshness of youth.
It is an early example of a chin-contouring device, a category that later included face straps and jaw exercisers.
quick.how: The advertisement shows a woman wearing the strap assembly and gripping cords, with the slogan urging readers to pull them. It was presumably used in repeated sessions at home.
quick.risks: No safety data from the period was found.

lead: Professor Mack's Chin Reducer and Beautifier was an 1890s chin-and-head strap device with pull cords. Its advertisement claimed it could remove double chins and reduce enlarged glands [1].
The printed address in the ad names Prof. Eugene Mack, 507 Fifth Avenue, New York. It aimed to help looks by slimming the area under the chin and giving a more defined profile [1].
Mental Floss includes it among bizarre old beauty contraptions, noting the ad said it worked provided the cords were pulled hard enough [1].

angle.text: The ad presented the device as a way to remove a double chin through pulled-cord tension. No test of its results was found.
